properties.name: Every store a process opens shares one RocksDB memory budget (--store-memory), measured before and after
properties.rationale:
req:one-open-design-costs-a-deliberate-amount-of-memory, on @ajs's word ("Yes, let's build the now items in reflow2").

MEASURED BEFORE AND AFTER, as the requirement demands, on four copies of reflow2's own design with MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2, debug builds of the same tree:
- per open design 41.0 → 36.3 MB, within the run-to-run spread;
- peak 294 → 289 MB;
- writes 6.0 → 6.0 per second.
The budget moved nothing measurable at this size, because RocksDB's buffers are not where a design's memory goes. A budget of 8 vs 512 MB moved the per-design cost by about 2 MB. What the ~36 MB IS is recorded as fact:a-reflow2-sized-open-design-costs-about-36mb-of-heap-and-rocksdb-is-not-most-of-it-2026-09-27: private heap taken at open, not yet attributed.

So this makes the store's share deliberate and bounded, the letter of the requirement's first sentence, at no measured cost. It does NOT make the whole per-design cost "a number somebody chose". The requirement stays accepted, not met.

The test was observed failing with the write-buffer manager unset: the second store's memtable was then charged nowhere.
